nodes.question: What was the role of aquafaba in the production of eggless gluten-free (ESGF) cakes?
nodes.answer: Aquafaba was used as a replacement for whole eggs in ESGF cakes, allowing for the creation of a gluten-free cake while maintaining similar textures and properties.
nodes.paragraph: Materials and Methods Materials The commercially canned chickpeas, haricot beans, and kidney beans were obtained from Tamek (Bursa, , Tur - key), and black-eyed peas were procured from Penguen (Bursa, Turkey), whose chemical compositions were given in Table S1. Aquafaba samples were drained through a stainless-steel sieve and separated from the seeds of com- mercially canned pulses, then stored at 4 . Xanthan gum (Ziboxan LD, Deosen Biochemical (Ordos) Ltd.) was provided by Tun kaya Chemical Substances (Istan- bul, Turkey). The whole eggs, rice flour, powdered sugar, sunflower oil, baking powder, vanillin, and iodized salt were bought from the local markets. Methanol, Folin Cio- calteu, hydroxymethylfurfural, acetic acid, ethyl acetate, sodium sulfate, and sodium carbonate were supplied from Merck Chemical Co. (Darmstadt, Germany). Gallic acid, 1,1-diphenyl-2-picrylhydrazyl, and furfural were supplied from Sigma Aldrich, (Darmstadt, Germany). Gluten free cake formulation and production The gluten-free control cake formula based on the rice flour weight was as follows: 100% whole eggs, 60% pow - dered sugar, 25% sunflower oil, 4% baking powder, 2% vanillin, 1% xanthan gum, and 0.5% salt.
